changes.evidence: One long descending initial stem with a low shoulder, followed by a small e and detached accent; no separate g-u sequence is visible. The fragment is not expanded into a word.
The d has an ascender and the following low loop is e, matching the nearby de forms; there is no separate u trough.
Both opening and closing marks are pairs of raised short strokes, not angular guillemets. This records the actual shape, not a difference between emphasis macros.
One separate wavy rule runs below the word. The manuscript has a single underline here, not two stacked rules. H emphasis and C underline are equivalent at the macro level.

changes.location: Interlinear insertion between i.e. and les
changes.evidence: A small word sits above the line with a guide curving into the gap before les. Its first compressed stroke and following low stroke, with a small mark above, favour où; the tiny letters do not become individually secure on enlargement.

The sequence shows the initial short i stroke and curled s-o, low compressed m-o-r, a descending p, tall h, dotted i, and the final s-m-e-s movement. Enlargement makes the word readable despite flattened small letters.
The two diagonal strokes occupy the full capital height, clearly larger than the surrounding small letters.

changes.location: Inline inverse expression, second X and exponent
changes.evidence: The second X is likewise full height. The raised short horizontal and separate upright are minus and 1; the intervening multiplication dot is a distinct low dot.
The upper stroke rises at its left, dips across the middle and turns upward at its right; a separate shorter near-straight stroke lies below. This is sufficient to read the wavy-over-bar relation.
A short c-o-m-m-e-n-t word occupies this space; its final tall t closes the compact word. No additional utative sequence is present.

changes.location: Via le fait que, abbreviation before Gr-cat.
changes.evidence: Two connected tall t-like uprights and a long low terminal e are visible. There are no separate o and u between the t strokes.
The first accented r-e movement, the d loop, low internal shoulders and final crossed tall stroke support réduit. The central letters remain highly compressed, so the C doubt is retained.
The detached accent has a short upper-left to lower-right stroke; the final s is a separate two-part turn. The enlarged ink supports the grave accent.

changes.h: \emph{strictes}; note mentions a wavy second underline
changes.evidence: A single independent rule sits under the word; this rule is appreciably straighter than the first occurrence. The note is considered as a description of ink, not text to import. No pure emphasis-macro difference is counted.

changes.location: Quotation marks around calcul des fractions
changes.evidence: Each end has two separate high strokes. They are manuscript double quotation marks, not drawn guillemets.
A low initial a is followed by a tall b; the o-u movement leads into the first t, a detached i dot, and the final upright t. The long shared cross-stroke is visible.
The word ends in a short e movement after the descending p. No additional s follows before the space leading to dans.
After 1 and a short dash, there are a c, a crossed t and a point. There is no a between c and t. Both closing parentheses are separately present in the full construction.

The glyph has a rounded lower bowl, an open upper-left portion and one horizontal crossbar. Its height approaches the nearby d and capital L, but the handwriting does not securely distinguish upper- and lower-case theta. A faint grey fleck just before the closer is not assigned punctuation.

changes.location: Right of L0 in the homomorphism diagram
changes.evidence: Two compact dark dots stand just to the right of L0, one above and slightly to the right of the other. They can be a colon; copying specks remain possible, so the mark is explicitly uncertain.

changes.location: Grey point above the right diagram object
changes.evidence: The separate point above the right part of L0 is diffuse and grey compared with both the object and the two dark punctuation-like dots. It supplies no identifiable letter, index or accent and is recorded here as an inspected surface mark.

changes.location: Prose line beneath the diagram, hom
changes.evidence: The word ends after m, and the space before de contains no baseline period. A low fleck beneath the word is not in the position of a terminal stop.

This independently inspected glyph has an upright left side, a rounded bowl and a horizontal bar. It is approximately the height of L. The same case ambiguity is recorded at the first occurrence; this subsequent occurrence uses its first candidate under the supplied recurrence convention.

changes.location: Action display, underlined Aut and low gr
changes.evidence: One independent horizontal rule lies beneath Aut. The small gr is lower and to the right; its g descender curves left below that rule and does not form another underline.

Several strong oblique cancellation strokes cross an underlying rounded form. Parts of a middle horizontal and a left upper upright favour theta, with case unresolved; 0 remains possible because some inner strokes may belong to the cancellation. Deletion itself is certain.

changes.location: Author page number at top centre
changes.evidence: One upright numeral 4 with its transverse stroke is present at the top centre; H explicitly records it in a note.
The separate lower-left digits read 149. They are represented only in the archive comment, with H note treated as an existing reading.

doubts.reason: Tiny two-part compressed writing with a small mark above; placement as an insertion is clear, letters remain imperfectly legible.
The d and terminal t support réduit but the internal compressed letters are not individually secure.

The rounded form and bar are readable, but case is not determined. A later occurrence was inspected separately and uses the first candidate under the recurrence convention; its own evidence is recorded in changes and notation.

doubts.location: Punctuation after right object of diagram
doubts.reason: The two dark dots are meaningful as a possible colon; their intentional status cannot be settled from this scan.
Oblique cancellation strokes partly obscure the inner bar and upper side. The reading is doubtful; deletion state is not.

notes: The whole source is 1685 × 2365 pixels. All source_bbox values are [left, top, right, bottom] in that original page, with right/bottom exclusive. Half a covers y=0..1261; half b covers y=1102..2364. The started time records the first timed visual-reading step after reading the supplied instructions and witnesses.

The page is a continuation beginning with the fragment pé, ending avec les. The author number is 4; the separate archive foliation is 149. No date is visible here. No missing opening or ending has been reconstructed from another page.
Author claim: the discussion is developed in Mme Sinh’s book under a chapter title about strict Gr-categories. The explicit qualification je pense belongs to the author and is preserved.

Author claims: associativity, unit and inverse isomorphisms are identities in the strict setting; an arbitrary Gr-category is Gr-equivalent to a strict one; a fractions construction connects the calculation with strict Gr-categories and is compared with the construction of derived categories. These are transcribed claims, not verified results.

Author description: the structure is a group in (1-ct.) and a 1-category in (Gr), described by (L1,L0,d,Θ), a group homomorphism d : L1 → L0 and an operation Θ : L0 → underlined Aut_gr(L1). The page does not yet give the conditions after avec les.

The inverse relation, each action-letter occurrence, all indices, arrowheads and the possible diagram punctuation prompted ink inspection. Mathematical expectation was not used to replace the written symbols. No proof check, re-proof, computation, formal certificate or background theorem check was performed; checks is therefore empty.

The two dark dots beside the homomorphism diagram are an uncovered possible punctuation mark, retained as an uncertain colon. A separate diffuse grey point above L0 has been recorded as an inspected surface mark rather than a new decoration. No implication or relation is inferred from these dots.

Both appearances of strictes and identités are singly underlined. The first strictes rule is visibly wavy and the second is straighter; their state is represented with the required uline macro and a comment. H editorial notes are not imported as manuscript text.

All eleven unresolved places were cropped once through out/scripts/crop.py at width 2800, default contrast 1.12 and zero rotation. No slanted or sideways note required rotation. The ordered view_log records the whole image, the two halves, then crops 01 through 11, each viewed once. Crop processing is logged in the reader evidence directory.

The final cancelled glyph has certain deletion state but doubtful content. A theta form is supported by the remaining bowl and bar; case and a possible zero are retained as alternatives. The character has not been replaced with a prose illegibility marker inside mathematics.

Final syntax and consistency validation passed: required report fields, permitted kinds, all source boxes, crop references, ordered image paths, TeX brace/dollar/display/environment balance and the five in-place doubt markers. A first validation attempt used an arbitrary size floor and rejected the complete 1348-byte reading; that size check was removed in favour of content checks. No compilation was run.

coverage: The whole page was viewed once for layout and each supplied full-resolution half once, sequentially, before eleven single close crops of genuinely unresolved loci. Every physical prose line, including words agreed by C and H, was compared with both complete witnesses. Accents, punctuation, word endings, abbreviation points, quotation pairs, the inline inverse expression, every quadruplet item, both arrows and their direction, all indices, the Aut underline and gr descender, the interlinear insertion, the bottom cancellation, page number and archive foliation were covered. The complete reading preserves both paragraphs, the two-object labelled horizontal diagram, the action display and the unfinished final line. H omits the interlinear word and leaves the cancelled symbol unreadable; both witnesses omit the possible colon beside the diagram. C doubts have individual resolution or retention entries, including those settled by a half. No other pages, other readers, outside text, OCR or compilation were used.
